stories.headline: Operator's 3D-to-sprite tooling reaches main, but source-scope review catches a gap
stories.summary: A versioned Operator 3D master and model-to-sprite tooling landed and the implementation packet was archived. The original independent review is blocked before reviewer launch because its source declaration omitted 12 of 22 changed paths. A separate exact-scope correction pair is ready; neither visual approval nor live gameplay integration is established.
stories.body: Commits 5afa6280 and f2d5f042 land the Operator ITER005 master provenance, inspection tools, static model-to-sprite pipeline and tests, and archive the implementation packet. Commit 26956c12 publishes an exact historical source-scope correction for 12 omitted paths among 22 changed paths. The packet says original review run 20261031T022410Z-7204104581e7 stopped at host validation before reviewer launch. Correction and independent-review packets are published, with review ready; correction implementation is not landed. No genuine accepted PASS, visual fidelity approval or in-game deployment is verified. Next owner: existing correction implementation owner, then separate reviewer.
bullets: Operator model-to-sprite implementation landed and archived.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN now has a committed foundation for turning the Operator's experimental 3D model into reproducible sprite candidates. The pipeline and source records have landed, but a review safeguard caught an incomplete declaration of the files involved. That prevents the original independent review from starting.

sections.heading: A more reproducible character pipeline
sections.text: The new tooling preserves a versioned experimental Operator master and provides inspection and static sprite-generation utilities. This is infrastructure for producing and comparing future character visuals, not a claim that a finished animation or playable character has been approved.

sections.heading: Why the reviewer could not begin
sections.text: The original review's host validator reconstructed 22 changed source paths, but 12 were absent from the archived packet's declaration. A newly published correction proposes to attest only those exact historical files and identities, without weakening the general check or replacing the original review run.

insights.title: Source provenance is now a practical art-pipeline gate
insights.explanation: The code can land while its independent review remains blocked by mismatched file accounting. For 3D assets, trustworthy source lineage matters alongside render quality.

insights.title: The correction preserves the original review identity
insights.explanation: The proposed exception is tied to immutable commits, file blobs and modes, and activates only after its own accepted independent review. It is not a blanket bypass.

article.takeaway: Operator 3D-to-sprite tooling is landed, but its original review and visual approval remain pending.
article.next_watch: Look for the exact source-scope correction implementation and independent PASS, then a fresh plan for the preserved original review run.

stories.headline: Receipt-recovery safeguard lands, moving a stalled review toward independent scrutiny
stories.summary: CUSTODIAN landed the archived-receipt capture recovery implementation and archived its task packet. It can plan a narrowly authenticated administrative receipt mirror, but the protected review has not been recovered or accepted. Its separate independent review remains ready.
stories.body: At main d4bd1f126346fb82554dd9a6557aaefb379854e1, commit 1f7c71191dc69ab61a8eed155533def427c41bcf adds source-bound receipt-capture planning and separately authorized apply, journal/replay protections, regression tests and lifecycle clarification. The archived implementation packet is complete; its summary reports 294 tests and 8/8 changed-file checks. Those are implementation-reported results, not an accepted independent review. The paired review packet remains ready. The original dual-disposition review run 20261031T005522Z-c70dd87f67a4 remains protected: no apply, canonical acceptance or host teardown was verified. Next owner: existing independent reviewer. Current CI conclusion and host worktree/lock/disk status are unverified.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN has landed a targeted safeguard for a review that reportedly passed but could not close because its archived receipt was missing. The new code can verify the original evidence and prepare a carefully bounded repair. It does not itself accept the review or authorize touching the protected run.

sections.heading: What the safeguard actually changes
sections.text: The recovery tool checks the original reviewer identity, recorded outcome and matching evidence before proposing an administrative receipt mirror. A separate authorization is required to apply it. The original reviewer-authored files must remain unchanged.

sections.heading: Why the finish line is still ahead
sections.text: The implementation is now in the main codebase and its task packet is archived. Its own independent reviewer has not yet delivered an accepted PASS. Passing implementation tests and landing code are distinct from independent acceptance and from running a recovery on the host.

insights.title: The repair can be reviewed without altering the protected review
insights.explanation: The new implementation uses synthetic tests and a separate apply gate. This makes it possible to scrutinize the recovery mechanism before deciding whether the original evidence should be reconciled.

insights.title: Closeout remains the bottleneck
insights.explanation: Until the independent review is accepted and the original run is separately authorized for recovery, the downstream administrator review chain remains gated. No clean worktree teardown is established.

article.takeaway: The receipt-recovery implementation has landed; its safety and correctness still require an independent accepted review before any protected recovery.
article.next_watch: Watch for an authenticated PASS and canonical closeout of the receipt-recovery review, then a separate authorization decision on the original run.

stories.headline: A recorded review PASS hits a missing-receipt barrier, prompting a targeted recovery plan
stories.summary: CUSTODIAN published a new recovery pair after its dual-disposition review reportedly produced a canonical PASS but could not close: the archived review packet lacks a matching independent-review receipt. The new packets are ready, not implemented. The original evidence and claim remain protected, and no accepted closeout or teardown is verified.
stories.body: At main f848228723513d21412aee0fdbd6bec6514db4e8, commits 6064d70 and f8482287 published and activated the agent-paired-review-archived-receipt-capture-recovery-v1 implementation packet and its independent review. The implementation packet reports that protected review run 20261031T005522Z-c70dd87f67a4 has an identity-bound canonical PASS and validated target receipt, but lacks the archived packet's Independent Review receipt. Coordinator finish rejects the mismatch. This is packet-reported host evidence, not an independently inspected host receipt or accepted review. The proposed implementation would verify exact identity and hashes, plan a coordinator-attributed mirror, and require separate authorization to apply it. The packets explicitly prohibit applying recovery to the protected run during implementation or review. No recovery code landing, independent acceptance, protected-run apply or canonical teardown is verified. GitHub-visible branches do not establish local process, lock, worktree or disk state. Next owner: existing implementation owner, then a separate reviewer; any later protected apply needs explicit authorization.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN's latest review appears to have reached a favorable verdict but not the finish line. A newly published task describes a narrow bookkeeping failure: the reviewer outcome and target receipt are present, while the matching receipt in the archived review packet is missing. Until that gap is reconciled, the system refuses to close the review.

sections.heading: Why a PASS is not yet an accepted review
sections.text: The task packet reports one completed independent reviewer turn with a canonical PASS. But CUSTODIAN's coordinator checks multiple matching records before accepting a review. Its finalization step stopped on the missing archived receipt. That is a protective refusal, not evidence that the underlying implementation failed.

sections.heading: A recovery that cannot rewrite the verdict
sections.text: The proposed change would first verify the exact run, source evidence and receipt hashes. Only a separately authorized operation could mirror the already authenticated receipt into the archive, clearly labeled as coordinator-produced administrative evidence. The original reviewer files and judgment must remain unchanged.

sections.heading: What this means for game development
sections.text: This is another closeout-system dependency rather than an Operator, art or gameplay feature. Resolving it could release a stalled review and help the project return attention to substantive development, but neither implementation nor protected recovery has happened yet.

insights.title: The bottleneck moved from review judgment to receipt reconciliation
insights.explanation: The new packet reports a PASS already recorded, yet canonical acceptance remains blocked by a missing second receipt. That narrows the reported failure mode, but the host evidence has not been independently inspected by this watch.

insights.title: A passing verdict does not authorize cleanup
insights.explanation: The review's claim, lock and worktree are explicitly preserved. No cleanup or disk recovery can be inferred until canonical finish and host teardown are proven.

article.takeaway: A specific review-closeout discrepancy is documented and a bounded recovery pair is ready. The review is not yet independently accepted, and no protected recovery has been authorized.
article.next_watch: Look for the recovery implementation landing, its own fresh independent review, and an authenticated closeout receipt before any separately authorized operation on the protected run.

stories.headline: Dual-disposition recovery lands on main; independent review is next gate
stories.summary: CUSTODIAN landed the exact-run dual-disposition recovery implementation and archived its implementation packet. The change adds digest-bound planning, evidence preservation and gated fresh-review continuation. Its paired independent review remains ready, not accepted. Protected original recovery is still unauthorized.
stories.body: Observed main: a696aef8d5aff23e9f2a477c85f1f792da6dcd02. Commit a696aef8 adds an exact-run plan/apply mechanism to paired_review_runner.py, synthetic tests and lifecycle documentation. The implementation packet moved to archived/ with Status: complete. The implementation summary reports 238 paired-runner tests, 69 workstream tests and 6/6 selected validation suites passing; an initial 90-second timeout was followed by two passing runs. These are implementation-reported local validation results, not a canonical independent PASS. The review packet review-agent-paired-review-dual-disposition-recovery-v1 remains ready and dependency-gated, and a GitHub diagnostic branch exists, but neither proves a reviewer is running. No accepted independent review receipt or verified host teardown was established. Protected run 20261030T191402Z-4dd067b9b8e2 has not been recovered; any plan/apply or fresh continuation requires separate explicit authorization after independent acceptance. Closeout ledger: implementation implemented, locally validated as reported, landed and archived; independent review pending; canonical host cleanup unknown. Next owner: existing independent review owner through authorized dispatcher. Blocker: independent accepted review and subsequent explicit authorization. GitHub-visible branch state does not establish Arch-local locks, worktrees or disk. Confirmed host worktree retired/retained counts and disk free/used: unknown; relay counts not freshly available. No verified superseded determination for held reviews.
